nodes.summary: For a formal power series $F \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ and natural numbers $k$ and $i$, let $m = k^i$; the power series $F(z^{k^i})$ is defined coefficientwise. When $m \ge 1$, its coefficient of $z^n$ is the coefficient of $z^{n/m}$ in $F$ if $m$ divides $n$, and $0$ otherwise; this is the substitution $z \mapsto z^m$ in $F$. nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $F \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ be a $k$-Mahler function. If $F$ is algebraic over $\mathbb{C}[z]$, that is, $P(F) = 0$ for some nonzero polynomial $P$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{C}[z]$, then $F$ is rational: there are polynomials $p, q \in \mathbb{C}[z]$ with $q \ne 0$ and $qF = p$ in $\mathbb{C}[[z]]$.
nodes.title: Nishioka's theorem: algebraic Mahler functions are rational
